item.title: Culinary Garden Cooking Classes at Quivira Vineyards — Sun Jul 19, 12:00 AM — Quivira Vineyards and Winery
item.description:
Join an immersive, hands-on culinary series at Quivira Vineyards, offered June 7-November 15 from 11 AM - 2 PM. Led by Estate Chef Julia, guests begin in the organic estate garden harvesting seasonal ingredients before moving to the open-air kitchen to prepare a garden-inspired, multi-course meal. This interactive experience highlights the connection between garden, vineyard, and kitchen, while teaching practical culinary techniques. The evening concludes with a shared meal paired with Quivira wines in a beautiful estate setting. Each date features a different focus, including handmade pasta, masa and tacos, stuffed pasta, global dumplings, and seasonal pie baking. Space is limited for these unique seasonal classes.

item.title: Ledson Summer Soirée — Sun Jul 19, 12:00 AM — Ledson Winery & Vineyards
item.description:
Ledson Summer Soirée at Ledson Winery & Vineyards returns July 17-19, 2026, for a memorable weekend celebrating the 110th birthday of Noble Ledson with exceptional wine, food, and family tradition. The festivities begin on Friday, July 17, from 5-7 PM with an intimate Winemaker Dinner at Stella Restaurant featuring a specially crafted menu and outstanding wines. On Saturday, July 18, from 6-8:30 PM, guests can enjoy a Progressive Wine & Food Pairing at Ledson Castle, showcasing six highly rated wines paired with dishes from Sonoma County chefs, followed by music and dancing beneath the stars. Throughout the celebration, wine tastings will be available July 16-19 from 10 AM-4 PM at Ledson Castle in Kenwood and Zina Lounge in Sonoma. This special weekend honors a remarkable family legacy through acclaimed wines, shared stories, and unforgettable experiences in the heart of Sonoma Valley.

item.title: Sonoma Coast Foraging Campout — Sun Jul 19, 12:00 AM — Sonoma Coast
item.description:
Sonoma Coast Foraging Campout is a 3-night immersive retreat on the Sonoma Coast featuring camping with hot showers, all meals made from fresh farm and foraged ingredients, and four days of hands-on ecological and foraging programming. The experience begins Thursday evening with dinner and concludes Sunday after brunch \(exact dates and times not specified\). Activities include seaweed harvesting and creating seaweed foot baths, sea urchin foraging, cooking and urchin art-making, guided walks focused on edible and medicinal plants, and sea salt harvesting with participants taking some home. Hosted by Fork In The Path, the retreat is designed for adventurous participants of all ages, offering a transformational nature-based experience that blends coastal ecology, foraging education, and shared communal meals along the Sonoma Coast.
Source: Press Democrat

item.title: Sundays in Sonoma at Viansa Winery — Sun Jul 19, 12:00 AM — Viansa Winery
item.description:
Viansa Winery feels made for live music, perched atop the Summit of Sonoma with sweeping vineyard views and Tuscan-inspired charm. This summer and fall, acclaimed singer-songwriter Greg Lamboy brings his warm, intimate sound to the hilltop terrace for select afternoon performances as part of Viansa's outdoor music series. An award-winning guitarist and frontman of the Americana band Pacific Standard, Lamboy is known for pitch-perfect melodies and deeply personal lyrics. His relaxed, soulful style pairs effortlessly with Viansa's panoramic setting, estate wines, and laid-back elegance. Settle in with a tasting, take in the views, and enjoy an afternoon where strong vocals, masterful guitar, and unforgettable songs rise above the everyday. Performance Dates: June 14, June 21, July 12, July 19, July 26, October 4, and October 18 from 12 pm -3 pm.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: Sonoma County Hot Air Balloon Classic — Sun Jul 19, 4:00 AM — Sonoma County Event Center at the Fairgrounds

Looking for a magical way to start your day? Join us for an unforgettable two-day Balloon Festival packed with fun for all ages!
4 AM Glow Show – Watch the sky come alive as glowing balloons flicker like fireflies in the early morning darkness. It’s a breathtaking sight you won’t want to miss!
FREE Kids Zone – After the glow show, let the little ones run wild with games and activities designed just for them.
Food & Vendors – Grab delicious bites, browse unique merchandise, and soak in the festive atmosphere while we prepare for potential balloon launches. Weather permitting.

Bring your friends, bring your family, and come create unforgettable memories together. Start your morning with wonder, laughter, and a sky full of color!
Don’t miss out—plan your visit today!

item.title: Introduction to Birds & Their Physiology — Sun Jul 19, 8:00 AM — Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
item.description:
Join Sugarloaf volunteer Steve Callow on this introduction to bird ID with an emphasis on their physiology. The outing begins at the main parking area and heads out Creekside Nature Trail and uphill to Hillside Trail. The group will have the option to complete the Hillside-Meadow loop or go as far as they'd like and backtrack to the main lot.
Tickets are $10 for general audiences, $5 for students, youth (12-17 year olds must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian), Sugarloaf members, Sugarloaf or RFO volunteers, and free for children 8-11. Not recommended for children younger than 8. **Tickets day-of on site are $15 and might not be available.** Wear comfortable clothing, appropriate footwear for rocky/slippery trails, and sun protection. Bring at least a quart of water, binoculars/birding guides (if you have them), and if you desire, a snack. Parking fees apply.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat, Visit Santa Rosa

item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Sun Jul 19, 8:00 AM — Marin County Civic Center
item.description:
Price: Free Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market. Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine. www.aginstitutemarin.org

item.title: Historic Trees at Jack London State Historic Park — Sun Jul 19, 9:00 AM — Jack London State Historic Park
item.description:
Join a 2.5-mile guided walk along historic trails through Beauty Ranch and down to the Wolf House ruins to explore the trees that helped shape Jack London’s property and vision for the land. Along the way, learn about London’s ambitious eucalyptus planting project, heritage orchard trees, and other notable specimens that have been part of the ranch’s landscape for generations.

item.description:
Office hours without the office! Having bid farewell to spring, we will be looking for summer-blooming species including larkspurs, monkeyflowers, clarkias, and lilies, and we will discuss the ecology of plant communities and how they respond to geology, fire, human interventions, and pollinators. Our route on the Lower Bald Mountain, Meadow, Hillside, and Creekside Nature Trails highlights the park's diverse landscapes and natural beauty while avoiding steep exposed climbs.
Meet at the main parking lot. Tickets are $10 for general audiences, $5 for students, youth (12-17 year olds must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian), Sugarloaf members, Sugarloaf or RFO volunteers, and free for children under 12.
